text: Name an evaluation metric for text generation or NLP
note: Scores for generated text, translation, summarisation, ASR, QA, parsing, tagging or LMs, incl. LLM-judge and factuality metrics. Not generic regression metrics.

answers.q: Modified n-gram precision times a brevity penalty. Over twenty years old and still the first number in every MT table.
Recall of n-grams or longest common subsequences against a reference summary. Summarisation's answer to BLEU.
The exponential of the average negative log-likelihood per token: roughly how many tokens the model is torn between.
Greedily matches tokens by cosine similarity of contextual embeddings. BLEU for people who want synonyms to count.
Harmonic mean of precision and recall. In SQuAD it is computed over the tokens the answer and reference share.

aka: Metric for Evaluation of Translation with Explicit ORdering
answers.q: Unigram matching that credits stems and synonyms, plus a fragmentation penalty. BLEU's cleverer, slower sibling.
(Substitutions + deletions + insertions) over reference words. Can exceed 100%, to everyone's embarrassment.

aka: Measuring the Gap Between Neural Text and Human Text using Divergence Frontiers
answers.q: Quantise embeddings of model text and human text, then trace the divergence frontier between them. NeurIPS 2021 Outstanding Paper.
The share of exact matches. Fine for classification, harsh for generation.
Right only if the string is identical to the reference, after lowercasing and stripping punctuation and articles.
WER's character-level sibling, kinder to languages where the "word" is a matter of opinion.
The average negative log-probability of each true token; perplexity is its exponential.
Similarity of embeddings by angle, as BERTScore uses for matching tokens.
The fewest insertions, deletions and substitutions that turn one string into another. Levenshtein, 1965.
Sample k programs: did at least one pass the unit tests? Chen et al. 2021 made it the code-generation standard.
Still the ground truth every automatic metric gets graded against.
Ask a strong model to grade the answers. Cheap, scalable, and fond of long replies and of itself.
F-score on character n-grams. Doesn't care how you tokenise, so morphologically rich languages like it.
Edits needed to turn the output into the reference, with block shifts counting as one move. Lower is better.

aka: Crosslingual Optimized Metric for Evaluation of Translation
answers.q: A learned MT metric: a multilingual encoder reads source, hypothesis and reference and regresses a human quality score.

aka: Bilingual Evaluation Understudy with Representations from Transformers
answers.q: A BERT fine-tuned to predict human ratings, after pre-training on millions of synthetic sentence pairs.
TF-IDF-weighted n-gram agreement with many reference captions, so boring words count for less.
Parses captions into scene graphs and scores the overlap of objects, attributes and relations.
Judges a caption by cosine similarity to the image in CLIP space. No reference captions needed.
Cross-entropy in bits per character or byte. The tokenizer-proof way to compare language models.
NER's scoring rule: an entity counts only if both its span and its type are exactly right.
BLEU with information weights, so rare n-grams count more. Named for the institute that ran the MT evaluations.
Two metrics share this name: Google's sentence-level min(precision, recall) BLEU variant, and one for grammatical error correction.
Simplification metric: rewards words correctly added, kept and deleted, judged against both the source and the references.
BLEU of each generation against all the others. High means the model keeps repeating itself: a diversity score.
Share of unique n-grams among the outputs: a diversity score from Li et al. 2016's dialogue paper.
BERTScore with optimal transport instead of greedy matching: earth mover's distance over contextual embeddings.
Evaluation as generation: how likely does BART think the output is, given the source or the reference?
Prompt GPT-4 with a rubric and chain of thought, then weight its scores by token probabilities.
Dependency parsing: the fraction of words assigned the correct head.
UAS, but the dependency label must be right too.
CoLA's metric: stays honest under class imbalance, where plain accuracy flatters.
STS-B's metric alongside Pearson: do the model's similarity scores rank sentence pairs like humans do?
Average of 1/rank of the first correct answer: retrieval and QA reward getting it near the top.
Graded relevance, discounted by log rank, normalised by the ideal ordering. BEIR reports nDCG@10.
Built for Japanese-English MT: scores word order by rank correlation, where BLEU barely notices reordering.
TER computed at the character level, normalised by the hypothesis length.
Semantic similarity of contextual embeddings, with variants that need no reference. Lo, 2019.
Judge a translation by whether semantic role fillers (who did what to whom) match, not by n-grams.
Lin and Och's 2004 metric for metrics: how well does a candidate metric rank the reference above the machine translations?
Scores MT by how likely a multilingual paraphraser finds the output given the reference. No human ratings needed.
COMET without the reference: quality estimation from the source and the translation alone.
COMET that also marks which spans are wrong, trained on both sentence ratings and MQM span annotations.
Human gold standard for MT: experts mark each error span with a category and severity, and the penalties are summed.
Checks a summary's consistency by running an NLI model over every source-sentence and summary-sentence pair.
A factual-consistency scorer trained on a unified "alignment" task built from many NLI, QA and paraphrase datasets.
Kryscinski et al. 2020: a classifier trained to spot summaries made inconsistent by rule-based corruptions.

aka: question answering and generation for summarization
Question Answering and Generation for Summarization
answers.q: Ask questions about the summary, answer them from the summary and from the source, and see whether the answers agree.
Factuality at the level of individual dependency arcs: is each arc in the summary entailed by the source?
Factual consistency for dialogue, via automatically generated questions and NLI.

aka: Fine-grained Atomic Evaluation of Factual Precision
answers.q: Break a long-form generation into atomic facts and report the share a knowledge source supports.
Hallucination check with no external source: sample the model again, and facts it can't repeat are probably invented.
Evaluation recast as yes/no Boolean questions answered by a T5, one per quality dimension.
Reference-free summary evaluation: builds a pseudo-reference from the source's most salient sentences.
How much does a summary help BERT fill in masked words in the source document?
Human summary evaluation that weights each content unit by how many reference summaries mention it.
Grusky et al. 2018: how much of a summary is copied from its article, and how long are the copied fragments?
Data-to-text metric that compares output with both the reference and the source table, so correct but unreferenced facts aren't punished.

aka: Referenced metric and Unreferenced metric Blended Evaluation Routine

answers.q: Evaluates a dialogue by what DialoGPT would say back, which needs no reference and no training data.

aka: Graph enhanced Representations for Automatic Dialogue Evaluation

answers.q: Rank replies by human feedback signals such as Reddit upvotes and replies.
Meena's human metric: is the reply sensible, and is it specific? "I don't know" is sensible and worthless.
BLEU plus weighted n-grams for keywords, AST matches and data-flow matches.
CodeBLEU's rival: drops the most common n-grams in a corpus, like boilerplate and punctuation, before scoring.
Text-to-SQL: run the predicted query and the reference, and compare the result tables.
Grammar-correction metric: finds the edit sequence that best matches the gold edits, then scores edit-level F0.5.

aka: Reference-less Sub-Metrics Optimized for Manual Evaluations of GEC
answers.q: Reference-less GEC metric: grammaticality, fluency and meaning-preservation sub-scores tuned to match human ratings.
AMR parsing's F1: finds the variable alignment that maximises triple overlap, a hill-climbing problem in itself.
Constituency parsing: F1 over labelled bracketed spans. The EVALB script has been in use since the 1990s.
CoNLL 2018 UD shared task: LAS, but content words must also have the right POS tag and morphology.
The oldest coreference metric (1995): counts the links needed to connect the chains. Lenient on big merges.
Coreference scoring that weighs each entity by its size and measures links within it, designed to fix MUC and B³'s quirks.
Caliskan et al. 2017: do "flower" and "insect" lean pleasant or unpleasant in embedding space, like in the human Implicit Association Test?
Earth mover's distance between two documents' word embeddings: how far must one text's words travel to become the other's?
Reference-free evaluation for retrieval-augmented generation: faithfulness, answer relevance and context quality, mostly scored by an LLM.
Readability from words per sentence and syllables per word, in US school grades. Simplification papers report it.
Unique words over total words. Falls as the text gets longer, which is why people invented MATTR and MTLD.
Probability that a human reader finds the text rude or disrespectful, from Jigsaw's classifier. RealToxicityPrompts used it to grade LMs.
Liu et al., 2017: the average of SPICE and CIDEr, used as a reward in policy-gradient captioning.
Chatbot Arena ranks LLMs from human head-to-head votes, first with online Elo and later with Bradley-Terry fits.

aka: average F1 of MUC, B3 and CEAF
answers.q: The OntoNotes coreference standard: the mean of the MUC, B³ and CEAFφ4 F1 scores.
